investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigation.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached the swarm's per-org remote agent cap and no new agents can be created. Because all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same agent-creation step as their entry point and all carry the identical 409 error message, the quota exhaustion is the single upstream blocker preventing any evidence from being collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard per-org remote agent quota of 100. The eval org used by the production-api observability probes has reached or exceeded that limit, causing POST /api/agents to return HTTP 409 ("conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100") before any agent is provisioned. Because the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339 calls createAgent as the first substantive step for all three remote-agents checks, none of the checks can proceed past agent creation, and all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remains unset. This is an eval infrastructure / environment-state failure: the production API endpoint itself is functioning (it returned a well-formed 409), but the eval org's quota is exhausted.

possibleCauses: Most likely: the eval org's remote agent count has accumulated to 100 due to prior eval runs that did not successfully clean up created agents (withCleanup may not have deleted agents on previous failures), leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
Possible: the eval org's quota was intentionally or accidentally lowered below the current number of existing remote agents, causing all new creation attempts to be rejected.
Possible: a previous eval run created agents but crashed or was interrupted before the cleanup/delete step ran, leaving stale agents that were never removed and now fill the quota.

Less likely: the quota limit of 100 was recently reduced at the swarm/backend level for the eval org specifically, though no source evidence supports a backend config change in the supplied artifacts.

Because the session could not be opened, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an image artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream SSE endpoint returned a 404 during session establishment in the production-api environment. The stream emitted a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation work could begin, which is why frameTypes contains only ["generation_start", "generation_error", "message"] and imageUrlPresent is false. This is an eval-infrastructure or runtime-harness availability failure localized to the production-api harness endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for this runtime environment, limiting its status-page impact.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigations.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached the swarm's per-org remote agent cap and no new agents can be created. Because all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same agent-creation step as their entry point and all carry the identical 409 error message, the quota exhaustion is the single upstream blocker preventing any evidence from being collected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard per-org remote agent quota of 100. The eval org used by the production-api observability probes has reached or exceeded that limit, causing POST /api/agents to return HTTP 409 ("conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100") before any agent is provisioned. Because the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339 calls createAgent as the first substantive step for all three remote-agents checks, none of the checks can proceed past agent creation, and all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remains unset. This is an eval infrastructure / environment-state failure: the production API endpoint itself is functioning (it returned a well-formed 409), but the eval org's quota is exhausted.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — all failing sibling IDs share the same message, confirming a single shared upstream dependency (agent creation) is the common failure point
possibleCauses: Most likely: the eval org's remote agent count has accumulated to 100 due to prior eval runs that did not successfully clean up created agents (withCleanup may not have deleted agents on previous failures), leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
Possible: the eval org's quota was intentionally or accidentally lowered below the current number of existing remote agents, causing all new creation attempts to be rejected.
Possible: a previous eval run created agents but crashed or was interrupted before the cleanup/delete step ran, leaving stale agents that were never removed and now fill the quota.

Less likely: the quota limit of 100 was recently reduced at the swarm/backend level for the eval org specifically, though no source evidence supports a backend config change in the supplied artifacts.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable at the time of the probe. Because the session could not be opened, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an image artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream SSE endpoint returned a 404 during session establishment in the production-api environment. The stream emitted a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation work could begin, which is why frameTypes contains only ["generation_start", "generation_error", "message"] and imageUrlPresent is false. This is an eval-infrastructure or runtime-harness availability failure localized to the production-api harness endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for this runtime environment, limiting its status-page impact.
